subject: Sixth Floor Health — Activation for new app teams & term tuning
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris@sixthfloorhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya@sfh-procurement.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sixth Floor Health — Activation for new app teams & term tuning

Hi Chris / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our conversation, Sixth Floor is planning to onboard three additional internal projects (Patient Intake, ClaimAssist, and Provider Portal) across April–June. To move forward we need two things from you: a) confirmation of the desired start windows for each project, and b) procurement guidance so we can align billing/terms.

Proposed ask from Redwood:
- Issue: Add 3 project-level API credentials (one per app) + 10 developer/test keys for each project (total 30 dev keys) by 2028-04-25.
- Capacity: Increase the committed baseline from 200k tokens/mo to 450k tokens/mo across the account for May–Dec (we can tier usage).
- Terms: Convert the current month-to-month arrangement into a 9-month committed term (May–Jan) at a blended unit price; in exchange Redwood will include a 12% volume discount and priority access to Dedicated burst capacity for scheduled launches.

I attached an updated SOW (SFH_SOW_v2.pdf) and a proposed rollout timeline (activation_timeline.xlsx). Can you confirm:
1) PO timeline (will procurement be able to sign off by Apr 22?)
2) Launch order — which project should we prioritize for the canary (we recommend Patient Intake first)
3) Any legal/term constraints we should be aware of (auto-renew, data residency asks, or SSO requirements)

If useful, I can put together a short one-page summary for procurement that calls out cost delta and the benefit of the committed term.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: SFH_SOW_v2.pdf
Attachment: activation_timeline.xlsx
From: Chris Nolan <chris@sixthfloorhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@sfh-procurement.com>, Procurement <procurement@sixthfloorhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sixth Floor Health — Activation for new app teams & term tuning

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary. Quick answers:
- PO timeline: Procurement is stretched this quarter but we're targeting Apr 24 for an internal approval meeting; final PO likely Apr 28 if there are no material changes. Priya, correct me if I'm off.
- Prioritization: Agree with Patient Intake as the canary, then Provider Portal, then ClaimAssist. We need the canary live by May 10 to meet product deadlines.
- Legal: We prefer a limited-term (9 months) vs auto-renew; also we need confirmation that logs/audit exports can be retained 180 days. No additional SSO requirements beyond existing SAML config.

Can you send a short procurement-friendly summary (line items: committed tokens, expected overage rate, discount level, list of API keys) that I can share with Finance?

On a separate note, is there flexibility on the start date for the extra dev/test keys? Some of our teams won't need all 30 immediately; could we stage issuance and keep the billing tied to the committed tokens?

—Chris
Chris Nolan
Director of Engineering, Sixth Floor Health
chris@sixthfloorhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Nolan <chris@sixthfloorhealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sixth Floor Health — Activation for new app teams & term tuning

Thanks — adding operational detail here.

Operational roll-out (high level):
1) Provisioning: We can pre-create the 3 project-level credentials and hold them inactive until teams request activation. Dev/test keys can be staged in three waves (10 keys/wave) — wave 1 for Patient Intake on Apr 25, wave 2 for Provider Portal on May 9, wave 3 for ClaimAssist on May 23.
2) Capacity & billing: We can bind the committed 450k tokens/mo to the account effective May 1. Billing will reflect the committed tier; overages billed at the published overage rate unless we agree to a blended rate in the SOW.
3) Canary plan: Patient Intake — Redwood will allocate a small Dedicated burst for 48 hours during the canary to ensure latency under load; we recommend smoke tests and one production-like run before May 10.
4) Security/compliance notes: We will provide weekly audit exports (CSV) for the 180-day retention ask; Naomi will coordinate the export format and S3 location.

Pricing note for the procurement summary: if SFH signs the 9-month commit (450k baseline) we can offer an effective 12% discount on unit price plus a 3% credit back if monthly usage exceeds the committed baseline by >20% for any month (applied to the following invoice). I'll draft a line-item table for Lauren to include in the procurement note.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
